3.0.s.en: (1) The generations of Moses and Aaron

3.0.1.en: The name of Moses has always come before that of his brother Aaron, since he was the prophet of God and the one He spoke with. In this chapter, however, the name of Aaron comes first, for the following reasons:

3.0.2.en: 1- All the discourse will be about the Levites and about matters relating to worship and to the priests who belong to Aaron. The sons of Moses did not share in the work of the priests, but were counted among the Levites of the clan of the Amramites, which belonged to the Kohathites.

3.0.3.en: 2- Because the historical order requires that the name of Aaron and his sons be written first, since he is the elder brother of Moses.

3.0.4.en: 3- It shows the humility of Moses, in that he did not exploit his position by mentioning his own name before his brother's, as long as the discourse was about the priesthood.

3.0.5.en: The expression "in the day that the Lord spake with Moses" takes us back to the same date on which the numbering began (ch. 1:1), which was the first day of the second month of the second year after the departure from Egypt.

3.1.0.en: Filling their hands: their ordination and their offering of the sacrifices with their own hands before the Lord.

3.1.1.en: The priest's office: the ministry of the priesthood.

3.1.2.en: The sons of Aaron were four, and their names are given according to the order of their birth: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar. Their names have been mentioned several times before in the books of Exodus and Leviticus. These four were chosen by God, and were consecrated and set apart for the holy ministry of the priesthood.

3.2.0.en: The Holy Spirit-inspired text returns to what was already mentioned in the Book of Leviticus (ch. 10:1, 2), because of the awesomeness of this event and to remind everyone of it: when the glory of the Lord came down upon the Tabernacle while Moses and Aaron were inside it, fire came down from God and consumed the holy burnt offering and kindled the altar. This divine fire became the source of every fire used in worship thereafter. The sin of Nadab and Abihu was that they did not use this divine fire, but used common fire which they brought in from outside, in carelessness and indifference toward the order that God had established. Therefore God's punishment was a deterrent: a divine fire came out from within the Tabernacle and consumed them at once. When they died they had no offspring to inherit the ministry after them, and so of the sons of Aaron only Eleazar and Ithamar remained, serving with their father before the Lord.

3.2.1.en: The Lord our God is long-suffering and patient with sinners, but He is also jealous for His Church and for the spirit of worship in it. So beware, beloved, of carelessness in dealing with God and His rights, and do not rely on God's mercies where they do not apply. Do not forget that the Lord Christ Himself, though He loves sinners and forgives adulterers, is also the One who rebuked the priests, the scribes and the Pharisees, and drove the sellers out of His house with the utmost firmness.

3.3.s.en: (2) The calling of the Levites to serve the house

3.3.0.en: Bring the tribe of Levi near: set apart and consecrate the Levites.

3.3.1.en: Before Aaron: preparing them to take part in the work with him.

3.3.2.en: That they may minister unto him: Aaron is to have the authority of organizing the worship.

3.3.3.en: The Lord commanded Moses to bring the males of the Levites, since God had chosen them and set them apart for the service of the Tabernacle, and declared that they would work under the leadership of Aaron the priest to help him in the ministry, with the tasks that would be entrusted to them afterward. The Levites here resemble the ministry of the deacons in the Church, who help the priests in the congregational worship and its arrangements, and who serve under their authority.

3.3.4.en: Here the mercies of God toward the tribe of Levi appear, whose father sinned in the incident at Shechem (Gen 34:25, 26). Yet through his repentance God turned his descendants to service, so that they became consecrated to God, and from them came the priesthood that leads the people in worship. Moreover, the Levites became a redemption and a substitute for the firstborn of the children of Israel (ch. 8). The Levites' adherence to the worship of God and their faith in Him appeared in the incident of the golden calf (Ex 32), when they obeyed Moses and slew those who insisted on worshiping the calf.

3.4.0.en: His charge: that is, the commands and directions of Aaron.

3.4.1.en: The charge of the whole congregation: that is, carrying out the ritual order for all the people.

3.4.2.en: The tabernacle: a word God used to describe the tent of meeting, as the dwelling in which He dwells in the midst of His people.

3.4.3.en: The first task that God appointed to the Levites was to receive the arrangements and rites of worship from Aaron with all precision and care, because they are also responsible before God for teaching these things and handing them on to the people and the whole congregation. The expression "to do the service of the tabernacle" is an introduction to the coming verses, in which God will explain some matters of this service.

3.5.0.en: The charge of the children of Israel: that is, they act on behalf of all the people in keeping the house of God.

3.5.1.en: The clans of the Levites, in their dwelling places, surrounded the Tabernacle, that is, they were between the Tabernacle and the tribes. Their first task was therefore to guard the Tabernacle, outwardly as a building, so that no one would approach it, and inwardly, all its contents, that is, its furnishings. This confirms that they alone were responsible for the service of the tabernacle.

3.6.0.en: The whole tribe of Levi is regarded as an offering from all the people to God, that is, a response to God's love and care. The children of Israel offered one tribe from among them to be consecrated to the service of God and His tabernacle, and they offered it to God by presenting it to Aaron, the leader of the priesthood, who then distributed them among the various services as the Lord commanded.

3.7.0.en: You shall appoint: you shall establish and assign work to him.

3.7.1.en: The stranger: any person who is not of the offspring of Aaron and the Levites, even if he is one of the people of God.

3.7.2.en: Aaron and his sons were to keep their priesthood. The meaning here is to carry out the priestly ministry and to preserve it and be zealous for it against the interference of any outsider.

3.7.3.en: God's warning was fearful to all the people: no one may approach this holy service except the priests of the house of Aaron, and whoever tries to encroach upon it or approach it shall be punished with death, as God Himself did with Korah and his brethren when they tried to offer incense to the Lord though they were not priests (this incident will be discussed in detail in ch. 16), and as He destroyed Uzzah, who touched the ark of the covenant of God (2 Sam 6:6, 7). Jewish tradition adds that the Jews afterward hung a golden sword on the outer door of the Tabernacle as a sign and reminder of this divine command that anyone who touches or deals with the Tabernacle and its holy things, other than the priests and the Levites, shall die.

3.7.4.en: My beloved brother ... perhaps you or one of the members of your family has received one of the ranks of the diaconate and has been called to serve the house of the Lord. Do not neglect this great service, then, and encourage your children also to commit themselves to it. There is nothing better than that God should set us apart as deacons to preserve order and worship in His house, for it is a great and honorable responsibility that the deacons, together with the priests, preserve the inheritance, the tradition and the rites of the Church.

3.8.s.en: (3) The Levites as the redemption of the firstborn of the people

3.8.0.en: And the Lord spoke to Moses: this expression means the continuation of the previous discourse, but it is an introduction to opening a new subject within the same discourse.

3.9.0.en: Here God, in His humility, explains to the people His wisdom in choosing the Levites for Himself and for His service. He takes the people's memory back to the time He smote the firstborn of the Egyptians, both of men and of beasts (Ex 12), and how God afterward commanded that all the firstborn of the people, of men and of beasts as well, be set apart for Him, since every one that opens the womb was a portion set apart for the Lord (Ex 13 ...). If the firstborn was an animal, it was offered as a sacrifice to God, but if it was a human being, five shekels of silver were offered in his place.

3.9.1.en: Here, however, after the building of the Tabernacle, God makes clear that the Levites became instead of the firstborn of the people. The words "the Levites shall be mine" are a new clarification of the special position of this tribe, of its belonging to God and of its service to Him.

3.9.2.en: Let us examine our hearts every day: are they truly consecrated to God and the dwelling place of His Holy Spirit? ... God set us apart for Himself and anointed our hearts with the oil of the Holy Myron when we received the sacrament of Baptism. But we must preserve this seal and this consecration, and remember that when God chose our hearts for His dwelling, they became His dwelling and His house alone, and it is not fitting for any stranger or foreigner, that is, any sin or lust, to dwell in it or come near it.

3.10.s.en: (4) The account of the clans of the Levites

3.10.0.en: After the numbering of the males of the people able to go to war from all the tribes (ch. 1), the Lord gave Moses a new charge, which was to number the males of the Levites, but from the age of one month and not from the age of 20 years, as for those who went out to war. This is because the men of the tribe of Levi who would serve God must be prepared from their childhood to be God's.

3.10.1.en: The Levites began their work from the age of 25 years until fifty (ch. 8:24, 25). God sanctified many of His prophets and saints in their earliest childhood: He called Jeremiah while he was in his mother's womb (Jer 1:5), and John the Baptist was also filled with the Spirit in his mother's womb, and the Church gives children entry into the first ranks of the diaconate, which is the Epsaltos, that is, the chanter.

3.10.2.en: This reminds us to care for our children from their childhood and to bind them to the Church, especially since she teaches us this through the sacrament of Baptism, which takes place at the beginning of their lives, and she commands us to give them spiritual care through partaking of the Holy Mysteries and through their attachment to the Church's schools of education.

3.11.0.en: Moses numbered the Levites as God commanded, mentioning the heads of their fathers' houses. It is noted that the heads of the clans of the Levites were three great men, sons of Levi the son of Jacob, and from these three came all the clans of the Levites. These three are mentioned in the order of their ages: "Gershon," the father of all the Gershonites; "Kohath," the origin of the clans of the Kohathites, who are the origin of Moses and Aaron; and the third is "Merari," from whom came all the tribes and clans of the Merarites.

3.12.0.en: After mentioning the sons of Levi, it mentions here the grandsons, who were eight, each of whom afterward founded a clan that bore his name. The two sons of Gershon were "Libni" and "Shimei," heads of their clans. The sons of Kohath were "Amram," "Izhar," "Hebron" and "Uzziel," and they became the heads of their clans. And the two sons of Merari were "Mahli" and "Mushi," likewise heads of their clans.

3.12.1.en: May we care about bringing up our children, because the traits of a person's character are formed in his early childhood. Caring for them is the most important work we offer them throughout their lives, and tenderness with guidance and sharing in their play is what forms in them a sound, stable and successful personality throughout life.

3.13.s.en: (5) The distribution of responsibilities among the clans of the Levites after they were numbered

3.13.0.en: As stated in (v. 18), Moses reminds us again that the clans of the "Libnites and the Shimites" belong to their father Gershon, and their number at the numbering was seven thousand five hundred males, from a month old and upward.

3.14.0.en: Just as God set for the tribes places and standards around the tent of meeting, here He fixes the place of the clans of the Gershonites, that their tents be on the west of the Tabernacle, that is, opposite the Holy of Holies (see the illustration at the end of the chapter). To organize their dwelling and work and to settle problems, "Eliasaph the son of Lael" was chosen as chief over all the Gershonites, that is, over both families together.

3.15.0.en: The work with which the two clans of the Gershonites were charged was the care of the Tabernacle, taking it apart and carrying it when journeying, and then putting it together again, that is, setting it up when encamping. The detail of their responsibility and charge was as follows:

3.15.1.en: 1- The tabernacle: the structure of the Tent, made of boards, pillars and bars, which formed its frame, and likewise the cloth curtains, which formed its walls, with their various beautiful colors (see Ex 26). The Gershonites were assigned to carry the cloth but not the wood of the tabernacle, since the wood was the portion of the "Merarites," as will come in (v. 36).

3.15.2.en: 2- The tent: the outer covering of the Tent, which was of goats' hair.

3.15.3.en: 3- The covering: this includes a covering of rams' skins and another of badgers' skins (a sea animal).

3.15.4.en: 4- The hanging for the door: the screen over the door of the tent of meeting, which was set up on five pillars.

3.15.5.en: 5- The hangings of the court: the linen curtains that surround the courtyard of the Tent and are hung on wooden pillars, so they were a wall for the Tent.

3.15.6.en: 6- The hanging for the door of the court: the screen that was on the door of the outer court on the east side.

3.15.7.en: 7- Its cords: the ropes used to fasten the parts of the Tent to one another and also used to stretch it to the pins.

3.15.8.en: 8- That which is around the tabernacle and around the altar: that is, the curtains that form the outer boundary, and likewise the inner curtains that divide the Tent into parts.

3.15.9.en: 9- All the service thereof: that is, all the other matters connected with the foregoing are in the charge of the Gershonites. (See the pictures of the Tabernacle and its contents in the second volume of the Encyclopedia of the Interpretation of the Old Testament, that is, the books of Exodus and Leviticus.)

3.16.0.en: The second group of the Levites, after the Gershonites, are the Kohathites, and the details of their clans are also given here for the second time: the Amramites (Amram is the father of Moses, Aaron and Miriam), the Izharites, the Hebronites, and finally the clan of the Uzzielites. The total number of males in these clans, from a month old, was eight thousand six hundred, and their task and responsibility was to keep the sanctuary and the Holy of Holies and their contents and to watch over them. The details will come in (v. 31).

3.17.0.en: As God did before in fixing the place of the Gershonites, so He does here also, and fixes the south of the Tabernacle as the place for the Kohathites, where they pitch their tents. He also chose a chief over all the clans of the Kohathites, "Elizaphan the son of Uzziel."

3.18.0.en: This verse gives the detail of the contents of the sanctuary and the Holy of Holies, to make clear the duties of the Kohathites.

3.18.1.en: 1- The ark: they carried it without touching it, by means of two staves, and they did not look at it, since the priests covered it before it was carried. It afterward contained the tables of the covenant, that is, the tables of the Law, and the rod of Aaron the priest, and the pot of manna. After the Tabernacle was set up, the place of the ark was in the Holy of Holies.

3.18.2.en: 2- The table: the table of the showbread (Ex 25:23), on which twelve loaves were placed, and its place was in the sanctuary. The priests also covered it before it was carried.

3.18.3.en: 3- The golden lampstand: see its description in (Ex 25:31). It too was covered, like those before it, before it was carried.

3.18.4.en: 4- The altars: these are the altar of burnt offering in the outer court and the golden altar of incense inside the sanctuary. The details of each altar and its use were already explained in the Book of Exodus.

3.18.5.en: 5- The vessels of the sanctuary: the small vessels and tools with which they minister, such as tongs and censers and other tools, or things larger in size, such as the laver.

3.18.6.en: 6- The veil and all the service thereof: that is, a summary of all the foregoing, meaning everything that is behind the veil and is used in the ritual service.

3.18.7.en: My beloved brother, our Church took over many of the arrangements that God Himself established for dividing the work between the priests and the deacons, as was the case anciently between the priests and the Levites. So preparing and arranging the tools of the altar became the responsibility of the deacons, but as for the holy vessels themselves, the deacon has no right to touch them with the bare hand, but only with wrappings, to hallow them and to honor their worth ... If the things of old in the Tabernacle had this dignity, how much more the vessels of the altar of the covenant of grace and redemption.

3.19.0.en: Chief over the chief of the Levites, with the oversight of them that keep the charge of the sanctuary: that is, the headship over all the chiefs of the Levites in what relates to the ritual work and worship.

3.19.1.en: Before God, Eleazar the son of Aaron was responsible for leading the work of the Levites, supervising their chiefs in the performance of their ministry and all their works.

3.20.0.en: The third group is the group of the "Merarites," which has the two clans of "the Mahlites and the Mushites." As was the case with the two previous groups ... the number of their males in the census is also mentioned here, which came to six thousand two hundred, and their chief is also mentioned, Zuriel the son of Abihail. As for the place of the clans of the Merarites, it was toward the north, as shown in the drawing at the end of the chapter.

3.21.0.en: As for their work and the responsibility with which God charged them, it was as follows:

3.21.1.en: 1- The boards of the tabernacle and its bars: the boards of the tabernacle are wooden boards made of acacia wood and overlaid with gold, and they formed the inner walls of the Tent (see Ex 26:15-29). The bars were the supports that fixed the boards and joined them to one another.

3.21.2.en: 2- Its sockets: the bases of the pillars, made of silver.

3.21.3.en: 3- All the vessels thereof and all the service thereof: that is, everything connected with the boards and the bars.

3.21.4.en: 4- The pillars of the court round about: that is, the wooden pillars of the outer court of the Tent, that is, the enclosure.

3.21.5.en: 5- Their sockets, and their pins, and their cords: their sockets, that is, the silver bases; and the pins are the wooden pieces that fix the pillars in the ground, inside and outside the Tent, and to which the pillars are drawn by the ropes, that is, the cords.

3.21.6.en: It is noted that the charge of the Merarites was the heaviest of the things in the Tent, and carrying it when journeying.

3.22.0.en: As for the last side, the east side, which is in front of the entrance of the door of the Tent, God assigned it to Moses the prophet and his brother Aaron the priest and their offspring. In origin Moses and Aaron are Levites of the group of the Kohathites, the clan of the Amramites, but they took a separate place, since Aaron came to represent the priesthood with his sons and Moses is the prophet of God. The responsibility that God entrusted to them with their sons was:

3.22.1.en: 1- Keeping the charge of the sanctuary: that is, the general and comprehensive care of the Tent and all that it contains and of the worship, and supervision of all the groups of the Levites. The expression "keeping the charge of the sanctuary" implicitly includes offering the sacrifices.

3.22.2.en: 2- For the charge of the children of Israel: that is, they act on behalf of all the people of Israel in preserving the holy things connected with the Tent.

3.22.3.en: 3- The stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death: the stranger here includes not only those foreign to the people but also anyone who is an outsider with no connection to the priesthood, even if he is of the people themselves. For in order to show His jealousy for His house, God forbade any person to enter and tamper with the holy things of the house, and so that the punishment might be a deterrent, He made it death.

3.23.0.en: This verse mentions the total number of the Levites in their three groups, which is twenty-two thousand ... whereas if we add these groups together we find them to be twenty-two thousand three hundred. It is said that the difference of three hundred were the firstborn of the Levites themselves, whom their fathers had redeemed first, together with all the firstborn of the tribes (Ex 13), before the numbering of the tribes, and for this reason they were excluded from the count here.

3.23.1.en: Let there be a definite ministry, even a small one, that you offer to God. For merely carrying the parts of the Tent was a great matter, so how much greater it will be if you offer a ministry to the Church, and the greatest ministry is to bring a person who is far away into her embrace.

3.24.s.en: (6) The Levites as a substitute for the firstborn of the people

3.24.0.en: The first numbering (ch. 1) was of the males of the people able to go to war, above the age of twenty years. The numbering that the Lord commanded Moses in this verse is like the numbering of the Levites, that is, from a month old and upward. This numbering was of the firstborn males only (v. 42), and He commanded him to write down this numbering of the males of the tribes, by numbers and names, for the sake of accuracy.

3.25.0.en: The purpose of this numbering was to substitute the firstborn of the Levites for the firstborn of all the people. To understand this point we shall explain it in detail ...

3.25.1.en: After the Lord slew the firstborn of the Egyptians, both of men and of beasts (Ex 12:29; Ex 13:1-2), He commanded the people that every firstborn be offered as a portion to the Lord, whether of the people's sons or of their beasts. By this new numbering God wished to relieve the people from offering their firstborn, and to set apart the firstborn of the Levites in place of the firstborn of the people.

3.25.2.en: And just as the men of the tribe of Levi were counted instead of the firstborn of the children of Israel, so too their beasts were all set apart for God instead of the firstborn of the beasts of the children of Israel.

3.26.0.en: When "Moses" finished numbering the firstborn by their names, their number was 22,273 (twenty-two thousand two hundred and seventy-three), that is, an excess of two hundred and seventy-three (273) over the number of the men of the Levites.

3.27.0.en: The numbers were very close, so the Lord commanded Moses to substitute the men of the tribe of Levi for the firstborn of the people, as a redemption for them, and likewise the beasts of the Levites for the firstborn of the beasts of the people, so that the Levites as a whole, and what they possess, become a portion for the Lord.

3.27.1.en: I am the Lord: a parenthetical expression whose purpose is to affirm that this command and this order have God alone as their source.

3.27.2.en: What an honor it is that God ascribes His own to His holy name. It is a glory that has been granted to us, since after Baptism we have all become His, bearing His seal. But, beloved, do you truly feel that your soul is consecrated to God and that everything you own is His? If you have not thought this way before, then remember from today that you are wholly God's, and that what you own is a gift from Him, so that you may manage it faithfully as His steward.

3.28.0.en: Shekel: it is considered the first weighed silver coin known to the people, and is estimated at about fifteen grams.

3.28.1.en: Gerah: this is 1/20 of the shekel, that is, the shekel equals 20 gerahs.

3.28.2.en: The shekel of the sanctuary: that is, the shekel exact in its weight (the standard). As for the surplus of the firstborn of the people who have no counterpart among the firstborn of the Levites, whose number is two hundred and seventy-three, their redemption is as follows:

3.28.3.en: Five silver shekels of exact weight are to be paid for each male, like the shekels kept with the priests, which represent the true weight, and it is mentioned that each shekel equals 20 gerahs, to confirm the weight and the value required. A question may arise here for some: on what basis were the two hundred and seventy-three who owed the silver ransom determined?

3.28.4.en: Although there are many opinions, the closest to reality is that the choice was made by one of the methods of casting lots with which all were satisfied, as a system that avoids partiality in choosing.

3.29.0.en: The total silver collected as a substitute and redemption for the firstborn of the people in excess of the Levites amounted to one thousand three hundred and sixty-five shekels, by the fixed weight, that is, the shekel of the sanctuary. Moses gave the silver that he had collected to Aaron and his sons the priests, as the Lord commanded, since they alone are responsible for the ministry and its needs.

3.29.1.en: The distribution of the service among the clans of the Levites when journeying
